Nigeria is our largest market, and we’re expanding across other emerging markets.

As Head of Lending Product, you’ll own Lending Product end to end. You’ll set the strategy, lead the product management team and be accountable for the customer experience and business outcomes. Your mandate is to grow consumer lending profitably while improving how well our credit products fit customers’ needs, protecting portfolio quality and increasing long-term customer value.

What you’ll own

  • Lending strategy and portfolio. Decide which customer segments, products and capabilities to prioritise across QuickLoan, Consumer Loan, RCL/FlexiCredit, Asset Finance and adjacent credit products. Keep QuickLoan as the product that serves customers at scale. Use revolving credit and loans for salaried customers to deepen relationships where those products meet borrowers’ needs. Stay close to borrowers through direct research and use funnel data, decline reasons, repayment behaviour, collections outcomes and customer support feedback to identify problems. Run experiments with clear success measures and use the results to decide what to scale, change or stop.
  • Product team leadership. Lead and develop the lending product managers. Give each PM clear ownership of outcomes, make explicit prioritisation decisions and align Engineering, Credit Risk, Data Science, Growth and Collections. How you’ll use AI

  • Work with Engineering to revisit delivery timelines and change how you scope, sequence and staff work so teams can ship and learn faster.

  • Turn practices that improve results into shared tools, playbooks and standards across the team.

Workstream economics and planning

Cross-functional delivery and governance

  • Define owners, milestones and expected economic impact

  • Set its roadmap, forecast, scorecard and operating cadence
  • Review peer analysis and improve analytical and implementation standards
  • Mentor other analysts where required
  • Document critical policy, model and decision-engine knowledge

  • Build the judgement and breadth required to progress into broader portfolio ownership

85F9662823.description:
About The Company

FairMoney is a pioneering mobile banking institution specializing in extending credit to emerging markets. Established in 2017, the company currently operates primarily within Nigeria, and it has secured nearly €50 million in funding from renowned global investors, including Tiger Global, DST, and Flourish Ventures.

In alignment with its vision, FairMoney is actively constructing the foremost mobile banking platform and point-of-sale (POS) solution tailored for emerging markets. The journey began with the introduction of a digital microcredit application exclusively available on Android and iOS devices.

Today, FairMoney has significantly expanded its range of services, encompassing a comprehensive suite of financial products, such as current accounts, savings accounts, debit cards, and state-of-the-art POS solutions designed to meet the needs of both merchants and agents. FairMoney thrives on its diverse workforce, bringing together talent from over 27 nationalities.

We operate at massive scale, move fast, and expect leaders to think in systems, not silos. Decisions are data-driven, accountability is explicit, and impact matters.

About The Role

We are hiring a Senior Risk Manager- Consumer Loans to own the credit risk of FairMoney's Consumer Loan product: larger, longer-tenor loans for salaried customers, underwritten on bank statements, verified income and credit bureau data. This role sits at the heart of how FairMoney decides who to lend to, how much to lend, at what price, and why.

The product is live and growing. This role exists to make sure it grows safely and profitably: the credit policy is clear, the credit engine does exactly what the policy says, and every rule is justified by its impact on sales and losses.

This is a senior, high-ownership role for someone who knows consumer credit deeply, is comfortable in the detail of rules and data, and can explain trade-offs simply to leadership.

Key Responsibilities

1. Credit Policy Ownership

    • Own the Consumer Loan credit policy end to end: eligibility, affordability (DTI), bureau categories, income verification, limits, pricing and tenor.
    • Keep the policy current and approved, with a clear record of every change and who signed it off.
    • Size every proposed rule in sales and risk before it goes live, and remove rules that cost sales without reducing losses.

2. Credit Engine & Underwriting Alignment

    • Make sure the credit engine implements the policy exactly. Regularly audit rules in production against the approved policy and close gaps.
    • Write clear rule specs for the credit engine team, review changes before release, and sign off test results.
    • Work with the Underwriting team on bank statement analysis, salary verification, employer checks and address verification, so manual decisions are consistent and fed back into the engine.

3. Portfolio Monitoring & Early Warning

    • Own weekly portfolio monitoring: approval rates, disbursement, vintage curves, DPD roll rates and losses, by segment and channel.
    • Set early warning triggers and act on them quickly (tighten, pause, re-price).
    • Measure expected vs actual performance for each policy change, and report what worked.

4. Growth with Discipline

    • Partner with Product, Sales and Unit Economics to grow volume within agreed loss and NPV targets.
    • Design and run controlled policy tests (limits, pricing, cut-offs) and scale what creates value.
    • Translate risk into simple trade-offs for leadership: sales gained or lost per month vs losses avoided.

5. Collections, Fraud & Governance

    • Close the loop with Collections: use repayment and recovery outcomes to improve policy.
    • Work with Fraud on identity, device and first-payment-default patterns.
    • Ensure the product meets CBN requirements and internal governance, with documented decisions and audit trail.

6. Culture, Ownership & Values

    • Operate as a self-starter and owner, not a task-taker.
    • Bring recommendations, not questions: "here is what we should do and what it does to sales and risk."
    • Stay calm under pressure and adaptable in a fast-changing environment.
    • Act with integrity, intellectual honesty, and accountability.
85F9662823.requirements:
Must-Have

  • 10+ years in consumer credit risk (personal loans, salary loans, cards or similar) at a bank, fintech or consumer lender.
  • Hands-on experience owning a credit policy and seeing it through to system implementation.
  • Strong grasp of affordability, bureau data (First Central, CRC, CreditRegistry or equivalents) and income verification.
  • Proven portfolio monitoring experience: vintages, roll rates, loss forecasting.
  • Strong SQL and Excel; comfortable working directly in data.
  • Clear, simple communicator with senior stakeholders.

Nice-To-Have

  • Experience with automated decision engines and rule testing.
  • Bank statement analytics or open banking experience.
  • Exposure to policy experiments and NPV-based decisions.
  • Python or similar.

What Success Looks Like

By Month 3

  • The credit policy is up to date, signed off, and matches what the credit engine does in production.
  • A weekly Consumer Loan risk pack is live, with early warning triggers agreed.
  • Every open policy gap has an owner, a fix date, and a sized sales and risk impact.

By Month 6

  • Policy changes are tested and measured as expected vs actual before scaling.
  • Consumer Loan volume is growing within agreed loss and NPV targets.
  • Leadership trusts the risk view enough to make fast decisions on limits, pricing and growth.

Final Note

This is not a reporting role. We want someone who owns the outcome, holds the line on risk when it matters, and backs growth when the numbers support it.

4BC5214A52.description:
FairMoney is a pioneering mobile banking institution specializing in extending credit to emerging markets. Established in 2017, the company currently operates primarily in Nigeria and has secured nearly €50 million in funding from renowned global investors, including Tiger Global, DST, and Flourish Ventures.

In alignment with its vision, FairMoney is actively constructing the foremost mobile banking platform and point-of-sale (POS) solution tailored for emerging markets. The journey began with the introduction of a digital microcredit application exclusively available on Android and iOS devices. Today, FairMoney has significantly expanded its range of services, encompassing a comprehensive suite of financial products, including current accounts, savings accounts, debit cards, and state-of-the-art point-of-sale (POS) solutions designed to meet the needs of both merchants and agents.

FairMoney thrives on its diverse workforce, bringing together talent from over 27 nationalities. This multicultural team drives the company’s mission of reshaping financial services for underserved communities.

To gain deeper insights into FairMoney’s pivotal role in reshaping Africa’s financial landscape, we invite you to watch an informative video.

Role Summary

  • The job holder will be involved in procedures that reduce credit risk in the organization, specifically management of early and deep bucket collections. 
  • He/she would work with the Collections Manager to monitor implemented processes for measurement of credit portfolio management. 

Key Responsibilities

  • Supervise the daily activities of the recovery team to ensure strong execution and accountability.
  • Coach, support, and monitor recovery team members for effective and efficient performance.
  • Review delinquent loan portfolios to identify default drivers, recovery gaps & emerging trends.
  • Recommend and track corrective actions to improve recovery outcomes and ensure timely closure of issues. 
  • Improve and optimize recovery processes for better efficiency and performance.
  • Prepare and review team performance and personnel monitoring reports. 
  • Manage administrative recovery activities, including regional drives allocation management.
  • Ensure recovery activities are carried out in line with company policy, regulatory expectations, and internal standards. 
  • Support the review and enhancement of collections policies, procedures, and standards to reflect best practice. 
  • Monitor recovery operations for emerging risks and recommend process improvements where needed, and provide regular portfolio recovery insights and collections updates to leadership.
  • Drive a culture of accountability, discipline, and customer-sensitive recovery practices within the team.
